_source: Branch Education Short 'The Flattest Surface in the World', watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-18: frames every ~3-4 s. No transcript panel on this Short, so line timings and word counts are estimated from the burned-in captions at ~150 words a minute. Our own descriptions.

hook.firstFrame: a small chrome-rimmed round mirror floating at an angle in a black-to-blue gradient
hook.firstLine: Asks whether something can be made truly flat

shots.picture: a round mirror with a polished metal rim turning slowly in a dark gradient
extreme close-up sliding along the mirror's polished edge
a large chip-printing machine in a grey hall with a floating title plate
inside the machine: a violet beam lands on a wafer on a moving stage
split view: the machine below, a macro of chip wiring and a beam cone above
machine cut open; the violet light path zigzags off a chain of mirrors toward the wafer
one curved mirror in close-up with a glowing tolerance number writing beside it
pull back to the whole machine with the mirror still glowing inside
the Earth beside the mirror on a starfield, same size, for a scale comparison
on a pale ground, tiny bumps compared with a person and a stack of objects for height
back to the floating round mirror in the dark gradient, as at the start

lines.gist: asks whether a perfectly flat surface can exist
says one does, and teases where it is used
names the chip-printing machine and what it copies onto wafers
the patterns are nanometre-scale wiring for microchips
light bounces off a chain of mirrors and any bump would blur the print
gives how tiny the mirrors' allowed bumps are
scales the mirror up to Earth's size to show how small its bumps would be
returns to calling it the flattest surface made

ending.lastFrame: the round mirror floating in the dark gradient, the same picture as the first frame

whyItWorks: opens on one mysterious object and a yes-or-no question, then reveals the machine it lives in
the light path is drawn as a glowing violet ribbon bouncing between parts of a cut-open machine
an impossible tolerance is made felt by scaling the part up to the size of the Earth
ends on the same floating object it opened with, so the Short loops
